sections.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
sections.abstract: These lecture notes introduce o-minimal structures through cell decomposition, dimension, definable triangulation, generic fibres, and smoothness.
sections.claimed_result: The author presents a six-chapter course treatment of tame geometry, including definable triangulation and generic-fibre results (arXiv abstract and HTML preface/contents).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Lecture notes on o-minimal expansions of the real field; the uploaded text identifies itself as November 1999 course notes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a 1999 course text newly deposited in 2026, not evidence of a new theorem; the preface says some topics, including VC theory, are omitted. Citation totals can reflect the underlying older material. Proofs were not audited.

sections.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
sections.abstract: These notes cover real-root counting, the Tarski–Seidenberg theorem, cylindrical algebraic decomposition, triangulation, and finiteness bounds for semialgebraic sets.
sections.claimed_result: The notes present algorithms and foundational results, including an explicit connected-component bound depending on equation degree and ambient dimension (arXiv abstract and HTML introduction).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Semialgebraic subsets of R^n defined by Boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities; the text identifies itself as October 2002 lecture notes.
sections.unique_caveat: The author explicitly says the content is not original; this is a 2002 exposition newly deposited in 2026, not a new research result. Current citation totals may reflect the old notes. Proofs were not audited.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: S2 reports 257 current citations (48 influential), score 14.998 (citation component 11.106; influential component 3.892). The 74.1/day current-total/arXiv-age proxy is not a window gain and is confounded by the notes’ October 2002 date. No HF upvotes or HN item.

sections.title: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
sections.abstract: The paper characterizes tangle matroids: a matroid with at least two elements is one exactly when three hyperplanes do not cover its ground set.
sections.claimed_result: The author states the characterization and derives, among other consequences, that no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Matroids with at least two elements; the theorem’s characterization uses covers by three hyperplanes.
sections.unique_caveat: The arXiv page gives a 2015 Annals of Combinatorics journal reference (19, 125–130); this is a newly deposited version of an established result, not a new 2026 theorem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: S2 reports 5 current citations (1 influential), score 4.277 (citation component 3.584; influential 0.693), the third-highest candidate score. Current total divided by the 3.60-day arXiv-record age is 1.39/day, not a period gain. The primary page’s 2015 journal reference downgrades this as new-window momentum; no HF/HN activity.

sections.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
sections.abstract: For a taut finite-depth foliation of a closed oriented atoroidal 3-manifold, the authors prove that only finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows are almost transverse to it up to orbit equivalence, and prove uniqueness when the flow has no perfect fits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say they prove Mosher’s Transverse Finiteness Conjecture and a rigidity theorem for the no-perfect-fits case (arXiv abstract and §1, Theorems 1.2–1.3).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed, oriented, atoroidal 3-manifold and finite-depth foliation; the uniqueness conclusion additionally assumes the flow has no perfect fits.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on the stated 3-manifold/foliation setting; the authors distinguish it from the broader finiteness conjecture for all pseudo-Anosov flows on such manifolds. This is an attributed preprint claim; no proof audit.

sections.title: Cylindrical Ricci flows and the PDE-ODI principle
sections.abstract: For ancient asymptotically cylindrical Ricci flows, the authors derive linear-versus-quadratic leading asymptotics, product-soliton rigidity in the linear case, and uniqueness of cylindrical tangent flows.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish asymptotics and cylindrical-region propagation using the PDE–ODI principle with a harmonic-map heat-flow gauge (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Ancient Ricci flows asymptotic to a cylinder; the product rigidity statement is for κ-solutions and is up to parabolic rescaling.
sections.unique_caveat: The results apply to the specified ancient asymptotically cylindrical setting; the proposed dimension-four surgery program is not completed by this paper. The 115-page preprint’s proofs were not independently checked.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: S2 reports 2 current citations (1 influential), one cross-list, score 3.140 (2.197 citation, 0.693 influential, 0.250 cross-list); current-total/5.11-day age is 0.39/day, not a period gain. No HF/HN activity.

sections.title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NIP groups
sections.abstract: For a global generically stable Keisler measure on a type-definable group in an NIP theory, idempotence is equivalent to being the unique translation-invariant measure on its type-definable stabilizer subgroup.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that this equivalence resolves the NIP case of the Idempotent Measure problem (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Global generically stable Keisler measures on type-definable groups in NIP theories.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem addresses the NIP/generically-stable setting only; it does not resolve the full Idempotent Measure problem outside these hypotheses.

sections.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
sections.abstract: Among fixed-area simple polygons with at most N sides, the regular N-gon uniquely maximizes area times the first positive Neumann eigenvalue, up to congruence.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state that this proves the polygonal Szegő–Weinberger conjecture and implies optimality of the triangular lattice’s Voronoi cell at fixed covolume (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Every integer N≥3; simple polygons of prescribed area with at most N sides; uniqueness is up to congruence.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is restricted to simple polygons and the first positive Neumann eigenvalue; it does not claim an analogous result for arbitrary planar domains.

sections.title: Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent
sections.abstract: For the isotropic L_p-Minkowski problem, the author proves uniqueness for p in a dimension-dependent interval immediately below the affine-invariant exponent −n−1.
sections.claimed_result: Uniform C^0 estimates and a spectral estimate for the Hilbert–Brunn–Minkowski operator yield uniqueness for p∈(−n−1−δ_n,−n−1), with δ_n>0 (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Solutions of the isotropic L_p-Minkowski problem in the supercritical range, for a dimension-dependent neighborhood below p=−n−1.
sections.unique_caveat: Uniqueness is proved only in a near-affine interval; the abstract does not claim uniqueness throughout the supercritical range p<−n−1.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: S2 reports 2 current citations and no influential citations, one cross-list, score 2.447 (2.197 citation, 0.250 cross-list); current-total/6.80-day age is 0.29/day, not period growth. No HF/HN activity.

sections.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
sections.abstract: For a linearly parameterized analytic system with a finite operator dictionary, coefficient recovery from one input–solution pair is possible exactly when the induced finite-dimensional recovery map is injective, and the authors prove a zero–one law for degenerate inputs.
sections.claimed_result: The authors characterize degenerate-input sets and apply the framework to matrices, analytic dynamical systems, and several ODE/PDE classes, identifying deterministic inputs that guarantee recovery in those classes (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite dictionaries of analytic operators and admissible inputs; the explicit deterministic guarantees are for several, not all, ODE/PDE classes.
sections.unique_caveat: The zero–one law is conditional on the defined admissible-input space and operator family; it is not a universal guarantee for arbitrary systems.

sections.title: Fractional minimality of the Simons cone for $s$ close to $1$
sections.abstract: The authors prove that the Simons cone in R^8 minimizes fractional perimeter under compact perturbations whenever s is sufficiently close to 1.
sections.claimed_result: The stated result is fractional-perimeter minimality of the Simons cone in dimension eight for orders sufficiently near 1 (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The fixed cone in R^8, compact perturbations, and s in an unspecified sufficiently-close-to-1 regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not quantify the admissible range of s; the claim is not for all fractional orders.

sections.title: Probabilistic well-posedness of dispersive PDEs beyond variance blowup II: quadratic nonlinear wave equation
sections.abstract: For the quadratic nonlinear wave equation on the two-dimensional torus with rough Gaussian data beyond the variance-blowup threshold, the authors obtain convergence in law after a vanishing multiplicative renormalization to a stochastic wave equation with zero initial data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors also report almost-sure finite-time blow-up of the limiting solution and convergence on every compact interval before its maximal existence time, using analysis of oscillatory second Picard iterates (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Quadratic NLW on T², rough Gaussian random initial data beyond the cited variance-blowup threshold, and times strictly before the limiting solution’s maximal existence time.
sections.unique_caveat: The convergence statement does not extend through the limiting solution’s finite blow-up time; the result depends on the stated random-data and renormalization framework.

sections.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
sections.abstract: Using oriented palette constructions and hypergraph containers, the authors derive lower bounds for hypergraph Ramsey numbers, including matching 2^{Θ_k(n log n)} bounds for the half-graph case.
sections.claimed_result: They answer a question of Mubayi and Suk affirmatively and obtain further tower-type Ramsey bounds for fixed parameter ranges (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-colour k-uniform hypergraph Ramsey numbers in the specific half-graph and other families; several bounds assume fixed k,t and the stated ranges.
sections.unique_caveat: The asymptotic bounds use fixed-parameter hypotheses and implicit constants; they are not uniform claims over all k,t.

sections.title: A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions
sections.abstract: For the specified Motzkin-path Hankel determinants, the author proves Cigler’s quadratic recurrence for every k≥0 and n≥2k+2 and also proves a companion determinant conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The recurrence is proved using Chebyshev polynomials, complementary minors, and a Plücker relation; the paper also independently proves that the determinant is independent of c (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Motzkin paths with level-step weights c+x at height zero and c above it; integers k≥0 and n≥2k+2.
sections.unique_caveat: The recurrence has the stated index and weight hypotheses; the companion determinant statement had also recently been proved independently by V. Jandhyala, as the abstract notes.

sections.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
sections.abstract: For quasi-split unramified groups, the author proves the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras and derives Waldspurger’s nonstandard version through a global geometric argument.
sections.claimed_result: The author’s abstract says the work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic and makes the endoscopic classification for classical groups unconditional (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Quasi-split unramified reductive groups; the proper finite-type Deligne–Mumford stack argument assumes anisotropic center, and the stated twisted consequence is in good characteristic.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a 190-page preprint with substantial technical dependencies; the broad downstream consequences are the author’s claims and were not independently verified here.
